\section[(dialogue)]{The body, health and family — a first pass}

\label{lesson:MR-R86-first-pass-the-body-health-and-family}



\begin{quote}
Say the words for sugar and salt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a hand, a foot, hair, a tooth, the throat
  \item the stomach, a shoulder, a finger, the neck, the face
  \item blood, a knee, the head, a fever, a clinic
  \item ill, pain, thirst, hunger, happy
  \item sad, a father, a mother, a son; a boy, a daughter; a girl
  \item a grandfather, a grandmother, an uncle, an aunt, an uncle
  \item a husband, a wife, a baby, a person, a woman
  \item a neighbour, a guest, a teacher, to hear, to get up
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A hand? (\textbf{\mr{हात}}, \emph{hāt}.) A foot? (\textbf{\mr{पाय}}, \emph{pāy}.) Hair? (\textbf{\mr{केस}}, \emph{kes}.) A tooth? (\textbf{\mr{दात}}, \emph{dāt}.) The throat? (\textbf{\mr{गळा}}, \emph{gaḷā}.) The stomach? (\textbf{\mr{पोट}}, \emph{poṭ}.) A shoulder? (\textbf{\mr{खांदा}}, \emph{khāndā}.) A finger? (\textbf{\mr{बोट}}, \emph{boṭ}.) The neck? (\textbf{\mr{मान}}, \emph{mān}.) The face? (\textbf{\mr{चेहरा}}, \emph{chehrā}.) Blood? (\textbf{\mr{रक्त}}, \emph{rakta}.) A knee? (\textbf{\mr{गुडघा}}, \emph{guḍghā}.) The head? (\textbf{\mr{डोके}}, \emph{ḍoke}.) A fever? (\textbf{\mr{ताप}}, \emph{tāp}.) A clinic? (\textbf{\mr{दवाखाना}}, \emph{davākhānā}.) Ill? (\textbf{\mr{आजारी}}, \emph{ājārī}.) Pain? (\textbf{\mr{वेदना}}, \emph{vedanā}.) Thirst? (\textbf{\mr{तहान}}, \emph{tahān}.) Hunger? (\textbf{\mr{भूक}}, \emph{bhūk}.) Happy? (\textbf{\mr{आनंदी}}, \emph{ānandī}.) Sad? (\textbf{\mr{दुःखी}}, \emph{duḥkhī}.) A father? (\textbf{\mr{वडील}}, \emph{vaḍīl}.) A mother? (\textbf{\mr{आई}}, \emph{āī}.) A son; a boy? (\textbf{\mr{मुलगा}}, \emph{mulgā}.) A daughter; a girl? (\textbf{\mr{मुलगी}}, \emph{mulgī}.) A grandfather? (\textbf{\mr{आजोबा}}, \emph{ājobā}.) A grandmother? (\textbf{\mr{आजी}}, \emph{ājī}.) An uncle? (\textbf{\mr{काका}}, \emph{kākā}.) An aunt? (\textbf{\mr{मावशी}}, \emph{māvshī}.) An uncle? (\textbf{\mr{मामा}}, \emph{māmā}.) A husband? (\textbf{\mr{नवरा}}, \emph{navrā}.) A wife? (\textbf{\mr{बायको}}, \emph{bāyko}.) A baby? (\textbf{\mr{बाळ}}, \emph{bāḷ}.) A person? (\textbf{\mr{माणूस}}, \emph{māṇūs}.) A woman? (\textbf{\mr{बाई}}, \emph{bāī}.) A neighbour? (\textbf{\mr{शेजारी}}, \emph{shejārī}.) A guest? (\textbf{\mr{पाहुणा}}, \emph{pāhuṇā}.) A teacher? (\textbf{\mr{शिक्षक}}, \emph{shikṣak}.) To hear? (\textbf{\mr{ऐकणे}}, \emph{aikṇe}.) To get up? (\textbf{\mr{उठणे}}, \emph{uṭhṇe}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Verbs, and the first foods — a second pass}

\label{lesson:MR-R86-second-pass-verbs-and-the-first-foods}



\begin{quote}
Say the words for to run and to play.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item to run, to play, to sell, to open, to cook
  \item to wash, to laugh, to cry, to sing; a song, to dance
  \item to forget, to send, to count, to catch, to cut
  \item to stop, to look for, to lose, to put on, to leave
  \item to throw, to fly, to swim, to teach, to make
  \item to lift, to pull, to push, to hide, to win
  \item to fill, to change, to hold, to fall, meat
  \item a fish, cooked rice, lentils, a fruit, an apple
  \item a banana, a potato, a carrot, sugar, salt
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To run? (\textbf{\mr{धावणे}}, \emph{dhāvṇe}.) To play? (\textbf{\mr{खेळणे}}, \emph{kheḷṇe}.) To sell? (\textbf{\mr{विकणे}}, \emph{vikṇe}.) To open? (\textbf{\mr{उघडणे}}, \emph{ughaḍṇe}.) To cook? (\textbf{\mr{शिजवणे}}, \emph{shijavṇe}.) To wash? (\textbf{\mr{धुणे}}, \emph{dhuṇe}.) To laugh? (\textbf{\mr{हसणे}}, \emph{hasṇe}.) To cry? (\textbf{\mr{रडणे}}, \emph{raḍṇe}.) To sing; a song? (\textbf{\mr{गाणे}}, \emph{gāṇe}.) To dance? (\textbf{\mr{नाचणे}}, \emph{nāchṇe}.) To forget? (\textbf{\mr{विसरणे}}, \emph{visarṇe}.) To send? (\textbf{\mr{पाठवणे}}, \emph{pāṭhavṇe}.) To count? (\textbf{\mr{मोजणे}}, \emph{mojṇe}.) To catch? (\textbf{\mr{पकडणे}}, \emph{pakaḍṇe}.) To cut? (\textbf{\mr{कापणे}}, \emph{kāpṇe}.) To stop? (\textbf{\mr{थांबणे}}, \emph{thāmbṇe}.) To look for? (\textbf{\mr{शोधणे}}, \emph{shodhṇe}.) To lose? (\textbf{\mr{हरवणे}}, \emph{haravṇe}.) To put on? (\textbf{\mr{घालणे}}, \emph{ghālṇe}.) To leave? (\textbf{\mr{सोडणे}}, \emph{soḍṇe}.) To throw? (\textbf{\mr{फेकणे}}, \emph{phekṇe}.) To fly? (\textbf{\mr{उडणे}}, \emph{uḍṇe}.) To swim? (\textbf{\mr{पोहणे}}, \emph{pohṇe}.) To teach? (\textbf{\mr{शिकवणे}}, \emph{shikavṇe}.) To make? (\textbf{\mr{बनवणे}}, \emph{banavṇe}.) To lift? (\textbf{\mr{उचलणे}}, \emph{uchalṇe}.) To pull? (\textbf{\mr{ओढणे}}, \emph{oḍhṇe}.) To push? (\textbf{\mr{ढकलणे}}, \emph{ḍhakalṇe}.) To hide? (\textbf{\mr{लपवणे}}, \emph{lapavṇe}.) To win? (\textbf{\mr{जिंकणे}}, \emph{jiṅkṇe}.) To fill? (\textbf{\mr{भरणे}}, \emph{bharṇe}.) To change? (\textbf{\mr{बदलणे}}, \emph{badalṇe}.) To hold? (\textbf{\mr{धरणे}}, \emph{dharṇe}.) To fall? (\textbf{\mr{पडणे}}, \emph{paḍṇe}.) Meat? (\textbf{\mr{मांस}}, \emph{māṁs}.) A fish? (\textbf{\mr{मासा}}, \emph{māsā}.) Cooked rice? (\textbf{\mr{भात}}, \emph{bhāt}.) Lentils? (\textbf{\mr{डाळ}}, \emph{ḍāḷ}.) A fruit? (\textbf{\mr{फळ}}, \emph{phaḷ}.) An apple? (\textbf{\mr{सफरचंद}}, \emph{safarchand}.) A banana? (\textbf{\mr{केळे}}, \emph{keḷe}.) A potato? (\textbf{\mr{बटाटा}}, \emph{baṭāṭā}.) A carrot? (\textbf{\mr{गाजर}}, \emph{gājar}.) Sugar? (\textbf{\mr{साखर}}, \emph{sākhar}.) Salt? (\textbf{\mr{मीठ}}, \emph{mīṭh}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
